column1: # Campaign 22 pd-client test evidence for pd-fallible-worker-lifecycle-runtime.

column8: The unique owner contains worker cancellation and join authority while cloned request handles share only request state. Full context propagation and cancellation parity remain open.
Bounded PD operations retain one worker and membership authority across retry, while explicit shutdown is owner-only. The complete upstream retry and option matrix remains open.

The Rust lifecycle fixture starts a real worker, rejects shutdown from a clone, and explicitly closes and joins through its unique owner. The upstream router suite setup and router behaviors remain open.
Owner shutdown closes the retained worker and reports terminal lifecycle failures instead of hiding them in Drop. Background EOF detection with no pending request remains open.
Explicit owner shutdown cancels retained work before close and join, with cloned handles unable to claim success. Background stream cancellation with no pending request remains open.
A broken retained TSO stream is retired under the shared worker and bounded request errors stay visible before owner shutdown. Full pending-request fan-out and EOF race parity remain open.
A cancelled retained TSO request does not transfer worker lifecycle authority and owner shutdown remains explicit. Full concurrent pending cancellation and batching parity remain open.
After owner shutdown, retained request handles observe closed state and cannot use or shut down the worker. Full service-client connection selection after close remains open.
